lines.text: A neatly dressed man with an easy manner comes out from the hallway to greet me with a polite smile.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Welcome, welcome! Not every day a man's car breaks down right in front of a motel. Lucky, in the unluckiest way possible.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I need a room for the night.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Of course. I'll give you room 4, it's the quietest one. If you need anything, any hour, my door's the first one by the lobby.
The kind of efficient manager you'd hope to find out on the highway. He clearly takes care of the place.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: A terrible business last night, detective. The Starlight has always been a peaceful place. I already notified the county sheriff first thing this morning.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You were fully dressed in your suit when you arrived at the scene in seconds.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: I was working late in my office reviewing supplier accounts with Mr. Vidal until past midnight. Running a business out here takes long hours.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: If you ask me, that vagrant Mark hangs around the gas station drinking cheap gin and gets aggressive in the dark.
An immaculate explanation, delivered without a single stutter. He deflects attention smoothly onto Mark.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I understand the building has a basement. What do you keep down there?

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: The machine room: backup generator, boilers, heavy tools. It's damp and hazardous, that's why I keep it padlocked.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Why do you ask, detective? If you need to inspect the motel's facilities, I'll gladly walk you through later.
A practical, professional answer. If he's hiding something, he covers it with the calm of a man used to managing everything himself.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Back to the basement: Elena told me you keep the only key to that door.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Of course. The boilers are old and the liability insurance is very strict. I can't have staff wandering down there.
Impeccable, from a business-management standpoint. But physical evidence will tell what really happened down there.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Elena told me you're the only one with a key to the basement.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: That's right. I handle the boilers and parts myself to avoid accidents. Basic safety protocol.
The explanation sounds reasonable and measured.

topics.displayName: Confront him with the motel evidence

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: The latch pried from the inside. Exclusive key access, yours alone. And Carla's travel bag hidden behind your toolboxes.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Those are very bold inferences, detective. A desperate drifter could have forced that lock, or planted those items to blackmail management.
For the first time, his polite smile vanishes. His eyes weigh every word of mine with icy calculation.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: If you have a formal accusation, I suggest you bring it to the sheriff with all the proof the law demands.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: The padlock was busted from the inside, and you're the only one with a key to that room.

lines.speaker: Robert
lines.text: Unfortunate coincidences, detective. But in a serious investigation, coincidences don't add up to a verdict.
He takes a measured second before answering. His facade holds, but the physical facts speak clearly.
